senior year in high school, I went to public schools. I wouldn't trade that
education and experience for anything.
 
I had incredible teachers. As I look at my life today, the things I value most
about myself- my imagination, my love of acting, my
passion for writing, my love of learning, my curiosity- all come from how I
was parented and taught.

much joy, that have brought me so much professional success- none of

questionText:
The recently launched Mission ShakthiSAT, is an ambitious initiative that
aims to empower young girls worldwide to excel in
space science, technology, engineering, and mathematics (STEM). This
historic all-girls mission, led by Space Kidz India (SKI),
involves a spacecraft journey from lunar-to-lunar orbit and will be part of
ISRO's Chandrayaan-4 mission in 2026. Through this
mission, SKI seeks to inspire young women to lead in space sciences and
demonstrate their potential in STEM fields.
 
Space Kidz India has a proven track record, having launched 19 Near
Space Launch Vehicles, 3 Suborbital Payloads, and 5 Orbital
Satellites. The mission's goal is to provide girls with the opportunity to
contribute to an actual space mission and witness their
satellite journey to the Moon. Srimathy Kesan, Founder and CEO of SKI,
emphasized that Mission ShakthiSAT is about creating a
global platform where young women can innovate and lead in space
sciences. The mission represents the limitless potential of
women and their role in shaping the future of space exploration.
 
Meridian Space Command, a UK-based company, has partnered with SKI
for mission management and in-space transportation.
Using its orbital transfer vehicle, Meridian will efficiently transport the
orbiter and lander to lunar orbit via PSLV, with a planned
crash landing on the Moon.
 
The ShaktiSAT programme also includes an online training curriculum on
space technology fundamentals, spacecraft systems,
and payload development. Following the online courses, 108 girls from 108
countries will be selected to participate in intensive
hands-on training in India, where they will collaborate to design, build, and
test a satellite for the mission.
 
How will the ShaktiSAT mission facilitate global collaboration in space?

By involving girl participants from 108 countries, for hands-on training in
India.

By building the first international space station in collaboration with
other space agencies.
By launching individual satellites from all the 108 countries involved.

By involving 108 countries in funding the ambitious and one of its kind
mission.

questionText:
One afternoon in late June, as the sun shone warmly into the large
courtyard, a very elegant Victoria, drawn by two sleek black
horses, stopped in front of the mansion. The Countess descended the
steps just as her husband, returning home, appeared at
the carriage entrance.
 
The Count paused, his face turning slightly pale as he observed his wife.
She was strikingly beautiful, with her long oval face, an

ivory-like complexion, large gray eyes, and jet-black hair. Her graceful and
aristocratic demeanour only heightened her appeal.
Without sparing him a glance or acknowledging his presence, she entered
the carriage with a high-bred air that rekindled the
burning jealousy which had long consumed him.
 
Approaching her, he asked in a measured tone, "You are going for a
drive?"
 
She responded coldly, "You see I am."
 
"May I join you?" he ventured, attempting to mask his unease.
 
"The carriage belongs to you," she replied disdainfully, her tone cutting
and dismissive.
 
Without reacting to her hostility, he climbed in and gave the order: "To the
Boulogne Woods" The footman took his place beside
the coachman, and the spirited horses pranced onto the street. Husband
and wife sat stiffly side by side in silence, the tension
between them palpable. He hesitated, seeking a way to begin a
conversation, but her resolute, icy demeanour held him back.
 
Finally, as if by accident, his gloved hand brushed hers. She recoiled
sharply, her gesture laden with unmistakable disgust. He
remained thoughtful, in spite of his usual authoritative and despotic
character, and finally said: "Gabrielle!"
What does the Count's behaviour throughout the scene suggest about his
personality?

He is authoritative and controlling but also vulnerable to jealousy
He is confident and not bothered about the Countess’s demeanour
He is carefree and uninterested in his wife's opinions or interests
